artifact.title: AI Infrastructure Stocks Slide as Selloff Hits Networking, Optics, Neoclouds
artifact.summary: Networking, optical and AI cloud stocks fell sharply on Friday, October 30, as investors reassessed the spending, financing and delivery schedules supporting the AI infrastructure buildout. Coherent dropped 11.3%, Marvell fell 10.0% and Arista Networks lost 8.3%. Neocloud providers also suffered substantial declines, with Nebius down 10.4%, CoreWeave down 9.7% and IREN down 8.8%. The losses extended across multiple layers of the infrastructure supply chain, from optical components and Ethernet switching to GPU cloud capacity. The retreat accompanied a broader technology selloff following hyperscaler earnings and renewed scrutiny of AI investment returns. The Nasdaq Composite declined 2.9% and the S&P 500 fell 1.8%, while Intel plunged nearly 29% after issuing a weaker-than-expected profit forecast. Networking and optical suppliers recorded losses substantially larger than the major indexes: Ciena fell 8.2%, Lumentum dropped 8.6% and Credo declined 8.7%. The breadth of the declines shows investors reducing exposure across interconnected AI infrastructure businesses, although individual share-price moves do not establish changes in customer orders. Microsoft’s results provided a concrete example of the deployment timing under scrutiny. The company reported $45.2 billion in quarterly capital expenditures, attributing the figure partly to delayed third-party capacity deliveries. artifact.title: CoreWeave Enters India with 240 MW AdaniConneX
artifact.summary: CoreWeave is entering India with plans for a 240 MW AI cloud deployment at the AdaniConneX Taloja campus in Navi Mumbai, establishing its first infrastructure footprint in the country and extending its international expansion into another major Asia-Pacific market. The deployment will span three 80 MW data center buildings, with CoreWeave serving as the sole tenant across the three facilities. The companies also envision an expansion option of up to another 240 MW at the campus, potentially bringing CoreWeave’s total footprint there to 480 MW. CoreWeave plans to deploy NVIDIA’s Vera Rubin platform at the site to support large-scale AI training, inference, reasoning and agentic workloads. The first phase is expected to become available in mid-2028, with additional capacity coming online in phases. artifact.title: CoreWeave Brings Up Multi-Rack NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Cluster
artifact.summary: CoreWeave has brought up a multi-rack NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 cluster on CoreWeave Cloud, connecting hundreds of Rubin GPUs into a Scale Out system for AI training, inference, reinforcement learning and agentic workloads. Each rack combines 72 Rubin GPUs, 36 Vera CPUs, NVLink 6, ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, BlueField-4 DPUs and a 45°C liquid-cooling design. NVLink 6 provides the intra-rack Scale Up fabric, while NVIDIA Spectrum-6 switches and the Spectrum-X Ethernet platform carry traffic between racks. CoreWeave did not disclose the number of racks, deployment location or customer-availability date. CoreWeave is treating the deployment as a unified system spanning compute, networking, power, cooling, firmware and software. Its automated bring-up process discovers new baseboard management controllers, verifies serial numbers, bootstraps credentials, updates firmware and moves nodes through staging and validation. CoreWeave Mission Control works with its Rack LifeCycle Controller, the Racky rack-management layer and Valvey liquid-cooling controls. Validation progresses from individual components and nodes to complete racks, the backend fabric and the multi-rack cluster. artifact.summary: Neoclouds — GPU-native public cloud platforms such as CoreWeave, Lambda, and Nebius — have emerged as a distinct alternative-hyperscaler category challenging AWS, GCP, and Azure for AI workloads in 2026.
